name: Skin Assessment
equipment: Visual inspection; well-lit environment; magnifying glass optional
steps: Inspect exposed skin areas: face, neck, forearms, hands, and any area under friction (waistband, collar).
Classify using the 4-category scale: Clear (no lesions), Mild (1–5 small lesions < 1 cm), Moderate (6–20 lesions or any lesion > 1 cm), Severe (> 20 lesions, open wounds, or spreading redness).
Photograph any lesion that was not present at the previous check-in and attach to the report.
when: Every 3 days, or immediately after any skin injury or unusual rash.
mistakes: Confusing dry skin (common in low-humidity cabin air) with an allergic or infectious rash. Dry skin has no raised borders or fluid.
escalate_if: Any rapidly spreading redness (> 5 cm diameter increase in 12 h), fever above 38 °C alongside a skin lesion, or pus discharge.
why: Microgravity and elevated radiation increase skin fragility. Immune suppression in space slows healing and raises infection risk from minor wounds.
benefits: Early classification prevents minor skin issues from progressing to infections that require systemic antibiotics.

actions.yellow: Apply prescribed topical moisturiser or barrier cream. Increase skin inspection frequency to daily. Document and photograph.
actions.red: Contact flight surgeon immediately. Begin wound care protocol. Isolate the affected area from further friction or contamination.

source_tag: NASA-STD-3001 Vol.1 §4.11; NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Skin Breakdown

name: Wound Healing Rate
equipment: Wound closure strips, sterile dressings, ruler or wound measurement tool
steps: On the day a wound is noted, record the date and photograph the wound with a scale reference.
Re-photograph every 48 hours. Measure the longest dimension of the open wound area.
Record how many days since wound onset when the wound is fully closed (epithelialised).
when: Starting at wound onset; re-assessed every 48 h until healed.
mistakes: Recording wound closure when a scab forms rather than when full epithelialisation is confirmed.
escalate_if: No measurable reduction in wound area after 7 days, or signs of infection (warmth, purulent discharge, increasing pain).
why: Wound healing is impaired in microgravity and under elevated radiation. Slow healing is an early systemic health indicator.
benefits: Tracking healing rate allows early antibiotic intervention, preventing mission-threatening infections.

actions.yellow: Increase wound care frequency. Apply silver-containing dressing if available. Report to flight surgeon.
actions.red: Ground consult mandatory. Begin systemic antibiotic protocol. Document and transmit wound photos.

source_tag: NASA-STD-3001 Vol.1 §4.11; NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Adverse Health Outcomes

name: Back Pain (VAS)
equipment: Visual Analogue Scale (printed card or digital slider); no additional equipment required
steps: At the same time each day (after waking), rate your overall back and spinal discomfort on a 0–10 scale (0 = no pain, 10 = worst imaginable pain).
Record the number in the check-in form.
If pain is localised, note the location (lumbar, thoracic, cervical) in the notes field.
when: Once per day, immediately after waking.
mistakes: Rating pain after exercise or physical therapy can underestimate chronic baseline pain.
escalate_if: Pain score ≥ 7 and not relieved by standard analgesics within 2 h, or any neurological symptoms (numbness, tingling, weakness in legs).
why: Spinal elongation in microgravity increases disc pressure and back pain. Bone density loss compounds the risk of vertebral compression fractures on return.
benefits: Daily VAS tracking identifies accelerating spinal stress before structural injury, enabling targeted exercise countermeasures.

actions.yellow: Increase resistive exercise frequency per exercise countermeasure protocol. Apply heat. Report to flight surgeon if score persists for 3 days.
actions.red: Restrict heavy lifting. Contact flight surgeon immediately. Begin diagnostic imaging protocol if available.

source_tag: NASA-STD-3001 Vol.1 §4.5; NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Bone Fracture

name: Grip Strength
steps: Sit or brace against a stable surface. Hold the dynamometer with the dominant hand, elbow at 90°.
Squeeze as hard as possible for 3 seconds. Record the peak value.
Repeat 3 times with a 1-minute rest between trials. Record the maximum of the three values.
when: Every 7 days, before exercise. Always use the dominant hand.
mistakes: Measuring after a workout gives falsely low results due to muscle fatigue. Wait at least 4 hours after vigorous exercise.
escalate_if: Drop of more than 20 % from personal baseline in a single week — indicates rapid muscle atrophy.
why: Grip strength is a validated proxy for overall muscle mass and systemic muscle atrophy, which is a key risk during extended microgravity exposure.
benefits: Weekly tracking allows the exercise countermeasure programme to be intensified before significant functional impairment occurs.

actions.yellow: Review and intensify resistive exercise protocol with flight surgeon. Add extra upper-body RED sessions.
actions.red: Report to flight surgeon immediately. Begin enhanced musculoskeletal assessment. Consider early mission modification.

source_tag: NASA-STD-3001 Vol.1 §4.5; NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Muscle Atrophy
